charm.land/bubbles.whatItIs: Bubbles, a set of ready-made parts for Bubble Tea terminal apps in the Go programming language, such as lists, text inputs and help lines.
goodAt: Adding a scrollable list a person can search by typing
Showing which keys do what at the bottom of the screen
notGoodAt: Running the app or drawing the screen; Bubble Tea does that.
charm.land/bubbles.example: A terminal app shows a list of open tickets that the user narrows down by typing part of a title.

charm.land/bubbletea.whatItIs: Bubble Tea, a library for the Go programming language for apps that fill the terminal window and react to each key a person presses.
goodAt: Building a full-screen terminal app with several screens
Keeping the screen in step with the app's data as keys arrive
notGoodAt: Commands that print a result and exit; a command library such as cobra fits.
charm.land/bubbletea.example: A person browses a list of tasks in the terminal with the arrow keys and opens one to read its notes.

charm.land/lipgloss.whatItIs: Lip Gloss, a library for the Go programming language that adds colors, borders and spacing to text shown in a terminal.
goodAt: Giving terminal text colors, bold titles and boxes
Lining up text in columns and panels
notGoodAt: Handling key presses or screens; Bubble Tea does that.
charm.land/lipgloss.example: A terminal app shows a task's title in bold purple and its status in green when it is done.

connectrpc.com/connect.whatItIs: Connect, a library for the Go programming language that serves and calls remote procedures defined in Protocol Buffers, answering gRPC, gRPC-Web and plain JSON requests on one port.
goodAt: Building a gRPC service on Go's standard web server
Letting browsers and curl call the same methods as gRPC clients
Generating typed clients and server interfaces from a schema file
notGoodAt: Plain JSON APIs designed around URLs and resources; a REST API stack fits better.
connectrpc.com/connect.example: A billing service exposes a CreateInvoice method that other Go services call over gRPC and a web page calls with JSON.

connectrpc.com/grpchealth.whatItIs: grpchealth, a Connect add-on that answers the standard gRPC health check, so load balancers and orchestrators can ask whether the service is ready.

connectrpc.com/grpcreflect.whatItIs: grpcreflect, a Connect add-on that lets tools such as grpcurl ask a running gRPC service which methods it has, without the schema files.

github.com/a-h/templ.whatItIs: templ, a library and code generator for the Go programming language that turns HTML components written in .templ files into Go functions, so the compiler checks every page's data.
goodAt: Building web pages from small reusable components
Catching a missing or misnamed value in a page when the code compiles
Escaping user text in HTML automatically
notGoodAt: Pages that run mostly in the browser; a JavaScript framework such as React fits better.
github.com/a-h/templ.example: An order page is a component that takes an order and its line items, and the build fails if the page uses a field the order doesn't have.

github.com/charmbracelet/x/exp/teatest.whatItIs: teatest, an experimental test helper that runs a Bubble Tea terminal app without a terminal, sends it key presses and checks what it shows.

github.com/jackc/pgx.whatItIs: pgx, a library for the Go programming language that reads and writes records in a PostgreSQL database.
goodAt: Letting a Go service read and save records in PostgreSQL
Running several database queries at once inside one program
notGoodAt: Changing a database's tables over time; use a tool for that, such as goose.
github.com/jackc/pgx.example: When a shopper's cart changes, a Go service saves it to PostgreSQL and loads it again when the shopper returns.

github.com/pressly/goose.whatItIs: goose, a tool and library for the Go programming language that records changes to a database's tables and applies them in order.
goodAt: Tracking which small database changes have already been applied
Bringing each copy of a database to the same table layout
notGoodAt: Deciding which tables the project needs; design those separately.
github.com/pressly/goose.example: When a team adds a table for customer reviews, goose creates it on every database in the same order.

github.com/PuerkitoBio/goquery.whatItIs: goquery, a Go library that reads an HTML page and finds parts of it with CSS selectors, often used to check pages in tests.

github.com/spf13/cobra.whatItIs: cobra, a library for the Go programming language, helps build programs you run by typing commands, each with its own options.
goodAt: Organizing a tool's commands and the options each one accepts
Showing a help message for each command
notGoodAt: Building a graphical interface with buttons and windows; use a desktop or web toolkit.
github.com/spf13/cobra.example: A deploy tool gets a status command, which prints a summary when a user types it, and a help message that lists its options.

github.com/spf13/viper.whatItIs: viper, a library for the Go programming language that gathers an app's settings from files and from the system it runs on, then combines them.
goodAt: Loading settings from files and the system a program runs on
Letting a single setting be overridden in a test or on a server
notGoodAt: Deciding the app's fallback values; set those in the program itself.
github.com/spf13/viper.example: When a team sets the address of an outside service in a settings file, the program reads it when it starts.

github.com/stretchr/testify.whatItIs: testify, a library for the Go programming language with ready-made checks for writing tests.
goodAt: Writing test checks that say clearly what a result should be
Checking that a function returns the expected error
notGoodAt: Running the tests themselves; Go's built-in test runner does that.
github.com/stretchr/testify.example: When a test sends an invalid order, a check confirms the program returns the error message the team expects.

go.yaml.in/yaml.whatItIs: go-yaml, a library for the Go programming language that reads and writes YAML, a plain-text format for settings files.
goodAt: Reading a settings file into the program's own types
Keeping names such as hostnames exactly as the user typed them
notGoodAt: Merging settings from files, flags and the environment; viper does that.
go.yaml.in/yaml.example: A command-line tool reads a list of servers from its settings file, keeping each server's name exactly as written.

golang.org/x/term.whatItIs: x/term, a library from the Go project that tells a program whether it is writing to a person's terminal or to a file.
goodAt: Showing colors only when a person is watching the terminal
Reading a password without showing it on screen
notGoodAt: Drawing full-screen terminal interfaces; use a terminal interface library.
golang.org/x/term.example: A command-line tool prints colored output in a terminal and plain text when its output goes to a file.

google.golang.org/protobuf.whatItIs: The official Go library for Protocol Buffers, a compact data format whose messages are described in schema files and turned into Go types.
goodAt: Sending structured messages between services in a small binary form
Keeping old and new versions of a message readable by each other
notGoodAt: Data people read or edit by hand; JSON or YAML is easier there.
google.golang.org/protobuf.example: An order service and a shipping service exchange order messages defined once in a shared schema file.
